---
name: evm-transactions
description: Load before buying a token or calling a contract on an EVM chain that evm_swap and bridge_usdc don't cover, before building any send_evm_transaction, and before telling the user a token can't be bought. Covers finding and pricing tokens, routing swaps, approvals, reading chains and gas.
---

# EVM transactions

`send_evm_transaction` sends a batch of calls you built from the user's EVM wallet.
Auni simulates it and the card shows what leaves and arrives. A trade or a claim goes on
a tap; sending assets away, trading tokens LI.FI can't price, getting back under half
the worth of what left, leaving a permission behind, a call Auni can't see do anything
(a vote, a lending switch), or a batch that can't be simulated takes the user's passkey. Use it when no other
tool fits; on Monad, Base, Arbitrum and Polygon, `evm_swap` buys tokens in one tap, and
`bridge_usdc` with `output_token` buys from cash on any chain Across reaches, in one tap.

Name the app the batch uses in `app` (Uniswap and uniswap.org, Aave and aave.com), with
`swap`, `deposit` or `move` when it is one, so the card wears that app's name and logo.
Make `summary` a short title that starts with what it does: "Stake ETH on Lido".

## Find and price the token

- Search DexScreener, no key needed:
  `curl -s "https://api.dexscreener.com/latest/dex/search?q=<name, symbol or address>"`.
  Each pair has its chain, the token's address, `liquidity.usd` and 24h volume. Take the
  address from the deepest pair on the chain the user means.
- A coin with its own chain usually trades on EVM chains wrapped, often as W plus its
  symbol (Pearl is WPRL on Ethereum). Search for that before saying it can't be bought.
- Price it with DefiLlama: `curl -s "https://coins.llama.fi/prices/current/<chain>:<address>"`,
  where chain is DefiLlama's name for it (ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, bsc...).
- A name with several tokens behind it, a pool with little liquidity, or a token
  launched days ago is worth one sentence to the user. Say it once, then propose.

## Read the chain

`read_chain` reads any EVM chain over JSON-RPC, a batch of calls at a time:
`{"chainId": 1, "calls": [{"method": "eth_call", "params": [{"to": "0x...", "data": "0x..."}, "latest"]}]}`.
Use it for balances, allowances, decimals and checking that an address is a contract.

## Route a swap through KyberSwap

1. Quote: `GET https://aggregator-api.kyberswap.com/<chain>/api/v1/routes?tokenIn=<addr>&tokenOut=<addr>&amountIn=<base units>`
   with header `x-client-id: auni`. `<chain>` is Kyber's name for it (ethereum,
   optimism, bsc...).
2. Build: `POST .../api/v1/route/build` with the same header and JSON
   `{"routeSummary": <data.routeSummary>, "sender": <wallet>, "recipient": <wallet>, "slippageTolerance": 100}`.
   The recipient is always the user's own wallet.
3. If the token in is an ERC-20, check the allowance for `routerAddress`. If it is
   short, first send `approve(routerAddress, amountIn)` to the token, first in the same
   batch as the swap. The exact amount is spent to zero, so the trade goes on a tap; a
   standing allowance the user asks for is fine, it just takes the passkey. On
   Ethereum each call is its own transaction, so an approval and a swap always take the
   passkey: sell a token there with `bridge_usdc` instead (see below).
4. The swap call: `to` is `routerAddress`, `data` the built calldata, `value` the
   built `transactionValue` in wei. `amount_usd` is what leaves the wallet in dollars.
   The calldata runs to thousands of characters: copy it whole, exactly as built. If Auni
   says a call reverts, quote and build again rather than patching the hex; routes also
   go stale within minutes.

The native coin is `0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE` in Kyber's routes.

## Gas

On a chain Auni doesn't list, the wallet pays its own gas in the chain's coin. Check that
balance with `eth_getBalance` first, and if it is empty or only dust, bridge a couple of
dollars of the coin there with `bridge_usdc` (`to_chain` the chain id, `output_token` the
zero address `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`), and tell the user once that it
pays for gas there.

## Getting money there

Cash is USDC on Monad, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon or Solana. To spend it elsewhere, bridge it with `bridge_usdc` to
the chain id first, as USDC or straight into the token. To sell a token anywhere else and
bring the money home, call `bridge_usdc` with `from_chain` its chain id,
`from_token` its address and `to_chain` monad: Across swaps it to USDC as it leaves, on one
card and one tap. Only when Across can't quote it, sell it for USDC on its chain (not USDT:
only USDC is cash) and bridge the USDC back.

Trade the amount the user names. If fees make another amount wiser (selling everything
in one go, say), suggest it in words, but the card is for what they asked.
